Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11

Class DamageAccumulator

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11.DamageAccumulator
public final class DamageAccumulator extends Object
Coalesces the damage rectangles reported for one composited window into a single bounding region, so the compositor reads back and re-uploads only the union of what actually changed instead of the whole window on every repaint (Phase E: damage-region readback + texture-upload batching).

Pure geometry with no X, no clock and no Java 3D state, so the coalescing is unit-testable headlessly. A live frame loop calls add(int, int, int, int) for every DamageNotify that arrives between frames, then drain() once per presented frame to get the single region to read; CompositedWindowPipeline does exactly this.

Coalescing to a bounding box (rather than tracking each rectangle) is the deliberate trade-off the compositor needs: one readback and one texture upload per frame, at the cost of re-reading the pixels between two far-apart damage rects. For the common case — a cursor blink, a scrolling list, a video frame — the damage is already contiguous, so the bounding box is tight.
